{{Short description|Category whose objects are finite sets and whose morphisms are functions}}
In the mathematical field of [[category theory]], '''FinSet''' is the [[category (mathematics)|category]] whose [[object (category theory)|object]]s are all [[finite set]]s and whose [[morphism]]s are all [[function (mathematics)|function]]s between them. '''FinOrd''' is the category whose objects are all [[finite ordinal number]]s and whose morphisms are all functions between 
them.

== Properties ==
'''FinSet''' is a [[full subcategory]] of '''[[Set (category)|Set]]''', the category whose objects are all sets and whose morphisms are all functions. Like '''Set''', '''FinSet''' is a [[large category]].

'''FinOrd''' is a full subcategory of '''FinSet''' as by the standard definition, suggested by [[John von Neumann]], each ordinal is the [[well-ordered set]] of all smaller ordinals. Unlike '''Set''' and '''FinSet''', '''FinOrd''' is a [[small category]].

'''FinOrd''' is a [[skeleton (category theory)|skeleton]] of '''FinSet'''. Therefore, '''FinSet''' and '''FinOrd''' are [[equivalent categories]].

== Topoi ==
Like '''Set''', '''FinSet''' and '''FinOrd''' are [[topos|topoi]]. As in '''Set''', in '''FinSet''' the [[categorical product]] of two objects ''A'' and ''B'' is given by the [[cartesian product]] {{nowrap|''A'' × ''B''}}, the [[categorical sum]] is given by the [[disjoint union]] {{nowrap|''A'' + ''B''}}, and the [[exponential object]] ''B''<sup>''A''</sup> is given by the set of all functions with [[domain of a function|domain]] ''A'' and [[codomain]] ''B''. In '''FinOrd''', the categorical product of two objects ''n'' and ''m'' is given by the [[product of ordinals|ordinal product]] {{nowrap|''n'' · ''m''}}, the categorical sum is given by the [[ordinal addition|ordinal sum]] {{nowrap|''n'' + ''m''}}, and the [[exponential object]] is given by the [[ordinal exponentiation]] ''n''<sup>''m''</sup>. The [[subobject classifier]] in '''FinSet''' and '''FinOrd''' is the same as in '''Set'''. '''FinOrd''' is an example of a [[PRO (category theory)|PRO]].
